text:
ConocoPhillips barely moved today, falling just 0.15%, after rallying 11.86% over the past two weeks. That two-week surge was driven by surging oil prices—crude has climbed sharply as Middle East tensions escalated, with Iran stepping up attacks on commercial shipping through the Strait of Hormuz and Saudi Aramco facilities coming under fire. Today's flat performance suggests the market has already priced in the near-term supply risk; oil prices dipped slightly as traders digested the IEA's plan to release over 20 million barrels of diesel to help ease record-high U.S. fuel costs.

The competing forces are clear: geopolitical risk pushes crude higher (good for an oil producer), but coordinated diesel releases by major economies push prices lower (bad for the upside). With U.S. crude at $96 and global crude at $125—a wide gap—the market appears to be balancing the immediate fear of supply cuts against the reality that governments are moving to stabilize fuel markets.
